label: GO after a rare-rewarded a1 trial (a1 -> S2 rewarded), late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1 or D2) when the previous trial was a1 that went rarely to S2 and was rewarded. That is the model-based switch-cue for a1 (rare-rewarded, so the agent should switch). It never fires on a2 rare-rewarded (a2 -> S1), so it is specific to the action and the transition. It is silent before ep_trial ~40 and its rate grows through the episode, so the episode-trial gate is part of the description. All variables are observed at GO, so no future variables are used. Missed activations are mostly low magnitude: some at rel -3 GO, where the previous trial falls outside the window and prev_* is unknown, and some weak firing after a2 -> S2 common rewarded (reward at S2 in general). The strongest activations are the clean a1 -> S2 rare-rewarded case. Activation is lower when the value estimate is high (none in the top value bin).

issues: Reproduced the reported test scores exactly: precision 0.938, recall 0.709, F1 0.808, mass recall 0.797.
'Fires only at GO' holds. On the dev split, D1 and D2 have 0 of 380,619 steps active each, and GO carries 100% of the activation mass.
'Never fires after a2 rare-rewarded' holds. GO & prev_reward==1 & prev_common==0 & prev_action==2 & ep_trial>=45 scored precision 0.0 with 9,697 steps predicted.
The feature always follows a rewarded previous trial: active on 0 steps where prev_reward==0.

The episode-trial condition is supported. The feature is silent for ep_trial 0-39. Its overall rate rises from 0.004 (trials 40-49) to 0.016 (trials 90-99). Inside the predicate, test precision is 0.62 for ep_trial 45-49, 0.93 for 50-69 and 0.997 for 70 and above. Without the ep_trial term, dev precision falls to 0.55.

The recall gap has two parts, and neither is a fixable systematic class. (a) The rel -3 GO step holds about 10% of the mass; there prev_* is unknown, and GO & rel==-3 & ep_trial>=45 has precision 0.02. (b) GO after a2 -> S2 common rewarded holds about 8% of the mass, but the feature fires there on only 2.5% of such steps. Restricting to good==1 raises that to 13%, still far too low to add. Widening to 'any rewarded S2 visit' gives F1 0.23, and adding low-value a2 -> S2 rewarded trials to the predicate drops test F1 to 0.56.

Within the predicate, firing does not depend much on the good state (precision 0.96 when good==1, 0.91 when good==2) or on the upcoming choice (precision 0.99 for a1, 0.90 for a2), so no hidden or upcoming variable is needed. False positives are scattered, mostly in the 45-50 trial onset region.
'Never in the top value-estimate bin' holds: 0 active steps when value >= 8.10.
